questions.question: Design a vending machine (LLD).
questions.title: Design a Vending Machine — Low-Level Design
questions.direct_answer: Model a vending machine as a **state machine** (`IDLE`, `ITEM_SELECTED`, `COIN_INSERTED`, `DISPENSING`, `OUT_OF_SERVICE`) driven by user actions (`selectItem`, `insertCoin`, `confirmPurchase`, `cancel`). The machine holds an `Inventory` (item slots with quantities), a `CashRegister` (denominations and counts), and a `PricingService`. Use the **State pattern** so each state cleanly owns the actions that are valid in it (no giant `if-else` over the current state). Refunds and change use a **greedy denomination algorithm** with a fallback if exact change isn't available. Concurrency: one user at a time per machine — a single mutex around the state transition is fine. Persistence is optional; for a network of machines, sync inventory + register to a central service.

interviewer_intent.testing: Modeling a clean state machine with the State pattern, separating inventory / cash / pricing concerns, change-making algorithm, and edge cases (out of stock, insufficient cash, exact change unavailable, mid-transaction cancel).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Giant switch/if-else over a `currentState` field with all logic in one class; ignoring exact-change failure mode; mixing inventory and cash in the same class.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Clean State pattern with one class per state; greedy change-making with explicit fallback; observability hooks; extensibility for cashless payments and remote refill.

sections.title: Problem Framing
sections.content:
A vending machine sells items for coins. The interesting design pressure is the **state machine** — the user goes through a sequence of actions, each valid only in certain states:

- `selectItem(code)` is valid in `IDLE` and `ITEM_SELECTED` (re-selection).
- `insertCoin(c)` is valid in `ITEM_SELECTED` and `COIN_INSERTED`.
- `confirmPurchase()` is valid only when enough money has been inserted.
- `cancel()` returns inserted coins and goes back to `IDLE`.

Mixed in: **inventory management** (item ran out), **cash handling** (machine ran out of small denominations for change), **pricing**, and **observability** (how often is each item sold, when does the machine need a refill).

This is the canonical small-OO design problem because the state-machine cleanliness is the entire grade.

sections.title: Clarifying Questions
sections.content:
- **Item types:** finite catalog with codes (A1, B2, ...), each with a price and quantity.
- **Payment:** coins only? Notes? Cards / UPI? (Card opens up async authorization.)
- **Change:** machine can return change in available denominations? What happens if it can't make exact change?
- **Refund:** can a user cancel mid-transaction?
- **Concurrency:** one user at a time per physical machine — confirm.
- **Persistence:** does machine state survive a restart? Or is it acceptable to lose the in-progress transaction?
- **Network of machines:** out of scope or in scope? (For interviews, usually one machine.)

sections.title: Assumptions
sections.content:
- Coins only (5, 10, 25, 50, 100 cents). Notes / cards called out as extensions.
- Finite item catalog by slot code (A1, A2, B1, B2, ...) with price + quantity.
- Machine attempts to return change in available denominations; if exact change can't be made, the purchase is refused and the inserted coins are refunded.
- Mid-transaction `cancel()` returns inserted coins and resets to `IDLE`.
- Single user at a time; one mutex protects state transitions.
- In-memory only for the interview; mention a `MachineRepository` interface for persistence.

sections.title: Core Entities and Responsibilities
sections.content:
- **`VendingMachine`** — facade exposing `selectItem`, `insertCoin`, `confirmPurchase`, `cancel`. Holds the current `State` and delegates to it.
- **`MachineState`** (interface) — one method per user action; default implementations throw `InvalidActionException` for actions not allowed in the current state.
- **State implementations:** `IdleState`, `ItemSelectedState`, `CoinInsertedState`, `DispensingState`, `OutOfServiceState`.
- **`Inventory`** — `Map<String, Slot>` keyed by slot code. `Slot` has `Item`, `quantity`. Knows `decrement`, `isInStock`.
- **`CashRegister`** — `Map<Denomination, Integer>` count by denomination. Methods `accept(coins)`, `dispense(amount) → Optional<List<Coin>>` returning coins for the requested change or empty if exact change unavailable.
- **`PricingService`** — simple lookup `Item → Money`; abstracted so promotions / dynamic pricing can drop in.
- **`Item`** — record (code, name).
- **`Money`** / **`Denomination`** value objects.

sections.title: Class Diagram
sections.content:
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class VendingMachine {
        -MachineState state
        -Inventory inventory
        -CashRegister register
        -PricingService pricing
        -Item selectedItem
        -List~Coin~ insertedCoins
        +selectItem(code)
        +insertCoin(coin)
        +confirmPurchase()
        +cancel()
        +setState(MachineState)
    }
    class MachineState {
        <<interface>>
        +selectItem(machine, code)
        +insertCoin(machine, coin)
        +confirmPurchase(machine)
        +cancel(machine)
    }
    class IdleState
    class ItemSelectedState
    class CoinInsertedState
    class DispensingState
    class OutOfServiceState

    class Inventory {
        -Map~String, Slot~ slots
        +get(code) Slot
        +decrement(code)
        +isInStock(code) bool
    }
    class CashRegister {
        -Map~Denomination, Integer~ counts
        +accept(coins)
        +makeChange(amount) Optional~List~Coin~~
    }
    class PricingService {
        +priceOf(Item) Money
    }

    VendingMachine --> MachineState
    VendingMachine --> Inventory
    VendingMachine --> CashRegister
    VendingMachine --> PricingService
    MachineState <|.. IdleState
    MachineState <|.. ItemSelectedState
    MachineState <|.. CoinInsertedState
    MachineState <|.. DispensingState
    MachineState <|.. OutOfServiceState
```

sections.title: State Diagram
sections.content:
```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> IDLE
    IDLE --> ITEM_SELECTED: selectItem(code)
    ITEM_SELECTED --> COIN_INSERTED: insertCoin
    ITEM_SELECTED --> IDLE: cancel
    COIN_INSERTED --> COIN_INSERTED: insertCoin
    COIN_INSERTED --> DISPENSING: confirmPurchase (enough money + can make change)
    COIN_INSERTED --> IDLE: cancel (refund coins)
    DISPENSING --> IDLE: item dispensed + change returned
    IDLE --> OUT_OF_SERVICE: maintenance / no power
    OUT_OF_SERVICE --> IDLE: cleared
```

Each state class enforces exactly which transitions are legal.

sections.title: Code — State Pattern + Core Methods
Change-Making Algorithm
Failure Modes and Edge Cases
sections.content:
- **Out of stock:** `selectItem` throws; UI prompts user to pick another item.
- **Insufficient funds at `confirmPurchase`:** stay in `COIN_INSERTED`; UI shows 'Insert another X cents.'
- **Exact change unavailable:** refund and abort. Light an 'Exact Change Only' indicator on items the machine can no longer give change for.
- **Cancel mid-transaction:** refund all inserted coins; reset to `IDLE`.
- **Power loss mid-dispense:** DISPENSING is the most dangerous state. Keep a small persistent log: `(transactionId, started, dispensed?)`. On reboot, if started but not dispensed — surface to operator and allow manual refund.
- **Item stuck in mechanism:** `DispensingState` should detect dispense failure (sensor) and either retry (one item over) or refund the difference and mark slot needing service.
- **Counterfeit / unrecognized coin:** the coin acceptor rejects before reaching `insertCoin`; never enters the machine's logic.
- **Maintenance:** `OutOfServiceState` rejects all user actions; only operator code can transition out.

sections.title: Extensibility
sections.content:
- **Cashless payment** (cards, UPI, NFC):
  - Add a `PaymentMethod` interface (`requestAuthorization`, `capture`, `refund`).
  - Replace `insertCoin` flow with `tap()` that requests authorization for the item price.
  - The state machine gains a `PAYMENT_AUTHORIZING` state between `ITEM_SELECTED` and `DISPENSING`.
- **Remote inventory monitoring:**
  - `Inventory.decrement` publishes `ItemSoldEvent`; subscriber pushes to a central service for restocking dashboards.
- **Promotions / dynamic pricing:**
  - `PricingService` becomes the extension point; no other code changes.
- **Multiple users (in a kiosk-style machine):**
  - Out of scope for a vending machine; if it became multi-user, you'd partition the state by lane and have one state machine per lane.
- **Network of machines:**
  - Each machine reports its state to a central service; central service issues firmware updates and pricing changes.

sections.title: Trade-offs and Alternatives
sections.content:
- **State pattern vs `enum` + switch:** State pattern is one class per state; enum + switch in `VendingMachine` works for tiny machines (4 states) but bloats fast and mixes responsibilities. Default to State.
- **Greedy vs DP change-making:** greedy is correct + cheap for canonical coin systems; DP is general but rarely needed.
- **Provisional vs deferred coin acceptance:** accepting coins into the register immediately (and refunding on cancel) is simpler than holding them in escrow; either works.
- **In-memory state vs persistent:** in-memory is fine if the machine has UPS / brief outage tolerance. For a real vending operator, sale logs and inventory must persist; introduce a `JournalingMachineRepository` and write transitions to flash.
- **Mutex vs lock-free:** one user per machine — a single mutex is correct and simple; no need for fancy concurrency control.

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **State pattern**: one class per state; each owns the actions valid in it.
- **Thin facade** (`VendingMachine`) delegates to the current state.
- **Separate `Inventory`, `CashRegister`, `PricingService`** — each changes for its own reason.
- **Greedy change-making on a copy**, commit only on success, refuse + refund on failure.
- **Single mutex** around the state transition; one user at a time per machine.
- **DISPENSING is the dangerous state** — journal transitions for crash recovery.
- **Cashless payments** drop in via a `PaymentMethod` interface and a new `PAYMENT_AUTHORIZING` state.
- **Operational signals:** `ItemSoldEvent`, register low, exact-change-only indicator.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**Problem framing**

Vending machine sells items for coins. Design pressure is the state machine — user goes through sequence, each action valid only in certain states.

selectItem valid in IDLE + ITEM_SELECTED. insertCoin valid in ITEM_SELECTED + COIN_INSERTED. confirmPurchase only when enough money inserted. cancel returns coins, back to IDLE.

Mixed in: inventory (item ran out), cash handling (machine ran out of small denominations for change), pricing, observability (how often each item sold, when refill needed).

Canonical small-OO problem because state-machine cleanliness is the entire grade.

**Clarifying questions**

Item types (catalog with codes, price, quantity). Payment (coins only? notes? cards/UPI?). Change handling (return change in available denominations? what if can't make exact?). Refund (cancel mid-transaction?). Concurrency (one user at a time per machine). Persistence (state survives restart?). Network of machines (in/out scope).

**Assumptions**

Coins only (5, 10, 25, 50, 100 cents). Notes/cards as extensions. Finite catalog by slot code with price + quantity. Machine returns change in available denominations; if can't, refuse purchase + refund. Mid-transaction cancel refunds. Single user at a time; one mutex. In-memory only; mention MachineRepository interface for persistence.

**Core entities**

VendingMachine: facade exposing selectItem, insertCoin, confirmPurchase, cancel. Holds current State, delegates.
MachineState interface: one method per user action; default impls throw InvalidActionException for actions not allowed in current state.
State impls: IdleState, ItemSelectedState, CoinInsertedState, DispensingState, OutOfServiceState.
Inventory: Map<String, Slot> by code. Slot has Item + quantity. decrement, isInStock.
CashRegister: Map<Denomination, Integer>. accept(coins), makeChange(amount) → Optional<List<Coin>>.
PricingService: lookup Item → Money; abstracted for promotions / dynamic pricing.

**State diagram**

IDLE → ITEM_SELECTED (selectItem) → COIN_INSERTED (insertCoin) → DISPENSING (confirmPurchase if enough money + can make change) → IDLE.

COIN_INSERTED → COIN_INSERTED (more coins). ITEM_SELECTED → IDLE (cancel). COIN_INSERTED → IDLE (cancel + refund).

IDLE ↔ OUT_OF_SERVICE for maintenance.

Each state class enforces which transitions are legal.

**Code — state pattern**

MachineState interface: default methods throw 'op not allowed in this state'.

IdleState.selectItem: checks inventory.isInStock, sets selected item, transitions to ItemSelectedState.

CoinInsertedState.insertCoin: m.acceptCoin(coin) — adds to insertedCoins, increments register provisionally.

CoinInsertedState.confirmPurchase: get price, sum inserted coins. If less than price → InsufficientFundsException. Compute changeAmount. register.makeChange(changeAmount). If empty Optional → refundInsertedCoins, IdleState, ExactChangeUnavailableException. Else → DispensingState, dispense item + return change, IdleState.

CoinInsertedState.cancel: refundInsertedCoins, IdleState.

VendingMachine itself thin: synchronized methods delegate to current state.

Keeps each state's logic local — no giant switch.

**Change-making algorithm**

Greedy denomination works for canonical coin systems (5, 10, 25, 50, 100).

makeChange(cents): copy counts. For each denomination descending, while cents >= d and available > 0, take coin, decrement available, decrement cents. If cents != 0 at end → Optional.empty (can't make exact). Else commit, return list.

Key points:
- Try on copy first; commit only on success. Half-completed change leaves register inconsistent
- Empty result → refuse purchase with ExactChangeUnavailableException + refund
- Unusual denominations: greedy can fail when DP would succeed; mention as extension
- Refunds use same algorithm; user's just-inserted coins as hint to give back same denominations preferentially

**Failure modes and edge cases**

- Out of stock: selectItem throws; UI prompts another item
- Insufficient funds at confirm: stay in COIN_INSERTED; UI shows 'insert another X cents'
- Exact change unavailable: refund + abort; light 'Exact Change Only' indicator on items that can no longer give change
- Cancel mid-transaction: refund + reset
- Power loss mid-dispense: DISPENSING is dangerous. Keep small persistent log (transactionId, started, dispensed?). On reboot, if started but not dispensed — surface to operator + allow manual refund
- Item stuck in mechanism: DispensingState detects dispense failure (sensor); retry (one item over) or refund difference + mark slot needs service
- Counterfeit coin: rejected by coin acceptor before reaching insertCoin; never enters logic
- Maintenance: OutOfServiceState rejects all user actions; only operator code transitions out

**Extensibility**

- Cashless payment: PaymentMethod interface (requestAuthorization, capture, refund). Replace insertCoin flow with tap() that requests auth for item price. State machine gains PAYMENT_AUTHORIZING state between ITEM_SELECTED and DISPENSING
- Remote inventory monitoring: Inventory.decrement publishes ItemSoldEvent; subscriber pushes to central service for restocking dashboards
- Promotions / dynamic pricing: PricingService is extension point; no other code changes
- Multi-user kiosk: out of scope; if needed, partition state by lane with one state machine per lane
- Network of machines: each machine reports state to central service; central issues firmware + pricing updates

**Trade-offs and alternatives**

- State pattern vs enum+switch: State pattern is one class per state; enum+switch works for tiny machines (4 states) but bloats fast and mixes responsibilities. Default to State
- Greedy vs DP change-making: greedy correct + cheap for canonical coin systems; DP general but rarely needed
- Provisional vs deferred coin acceptance: accepting into register immediately (refund on cancel) is simpler than escrow
- In-memory vs persistent: in-memory fine with UPS / brief outage tolerance; real operator needs sales logs + inventory persisted; JournalingMachineRepository writes transitions to flash
- Mutex vs lock-free: one user per machine — single mutex is correct and simple

**Recommendation**

**Use the State pattern with one class per state — IdleState, ItemSelectedState, CoinInsertedState, DispensingState, OutOfServiceState — so each state owns exactly the actions valid in it. Keep VendingMachine as a thin facade that delegates to the current state under a single mutex. Separate Inventory, CashRegister, and PricingService so each changes for its own reason. Use greedy change-making on a copy, commit only on success, refuse + refund when exact change isn't possible. Journal DISPENSING transitions for crash recovery. Cashless payments drop in via a PaymentMethod interface and one new state. Operational signals (ItemSoldEvent, register low, exact-change-only indicator) emerge naturally.**

followup_questions: Why is the State pattern preferred over a giant switch on `currentState`?
Walk through your change-making logic when greedy would fail — when does that happen?
How would you add cashless payments (card / UPI) to this design?
How do you recover state safely after a power loss in the middle of dispensing?
